import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import pandas as pd

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Convert 'StichtagDat' to datetime
data['StichtagDat'] = pd.to_datetime(data['StichtagDat'])

# Create a bar chart to show the most common breeds
breed_counts = data['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().head(10)
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.barplot(x=breed_counts.index, y=breed_counts.values, palette='Blues')
plt.title('10 Most Common Breeds in Zurich')
plt.xlabel('Breed')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.xticks(rotation=90)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output_breeds.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
plt.clf()

# Create a histogram to show the age distribution of dogs
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.histplot(data['AlterV10Sort'], bins=10, kde=True)
plt.title('Age Distribution of Dogs in Zurich')
plt.xlabel('Age (Years)')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output_age.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
plt.clf()

# Create a pie chart to show the distribution of male and female dogs
male_count = (data['SexHundCd'] == 1).sum()
female_count = (data['SexHundCd'] == 2).sum()
other_count = len(data) - male_count - female_count
labels = ['Male', 'Female', 'Other']
sizes = [male_count, female_count, other_count]
plt.figure(figsize=(8,8))
plt.pie(sizes, labels=labels, autopct='%1.1f%%')
plt.title('Sex Distribution of Dogs in Zurich')
plt.axis('equal')  # Equal aspect ratio ensures that pie is drawn as a circle.
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output_sex.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
plt.clf()

# Create a scatter plot to show the relationship between age and weight
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.scatterplot(x=data['AlterV10Sort'], y=data['AlterVHundNum'])
plt.title('Relationship between Age and Weight of Dogs in Zurich')
plt.xlabel('Age (Years)')
plt.ylabel('Weight (kg)')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output_age_weight.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
plt.clf()
